Put finished genuine wine in storage and a battery in the power slot. Each productive night consumes power, advances wine aging, and chills the wine. Empty or unpowered machines do not perform machine aging.

Modules: 6×20; storage: 20×20. Machine aging is 1 + floor(max(0, quality)/125) days per cycle: 125 quality gives 2 days; 1000 gives 9. Natural aging is separate.

Base power is 24kJ per productive night for the whole machine, not per bottle. Quality does not directly add power at each 125-point threshold. Modules also carry power, efficiency, or performance effects: +100% extra consumption adds 24kJ to the base; efficiency and performance may reduce it. Native rounding and the minimum of 1kJ apply. See the current values below.

Insert four identical supported fruits to produce one matching pulp. Different fruits cannot be mixed into one pulp; output space is required. Supports this mod's concentrate-ready fruits and native wine berries.

The manual button costs no energy and works without a battery. With a charged battery, material insertion or cleared output triggers automatic production at 8kJ per pulp. Missing material, space, or power prevents completion.

Use the xuxu Transfer Line to connect to an xuxu Brewing Barrel in either selection order. Pulp automatically moves to its pulp intake. A full destination retains the pulp in the concentrator until space opens.

Place two valid pulps in the pulp intake, native empty wine bottles in the bottle intake, usable yeast in the yeast intake, and enough water; then start brewing. Each bottle uses 750ml and one use from each pulp. Fresh pulp has four uses; a batch starts up to four bottles and needs up to 3L. The fruit pair selects the recipe; yeast follows native fermentation rules.

Finished bottles move to output automatically. Full output retains them until space is available. Clear the previous output before another batch. Water toxicity and euphoria are retained. The barrel itself has no battery.

Connect a concentrator, wine-bottle printer, or water container using the Transfer Line in either order. Missing water refills automatically; pulp and bottles fill available space. The linked print button uses the printer battery: four bottles for 20kJ.

Insert a charged battery and press Print: each action costs 20kJ and produces four native empty wine bottles. Output is 4×4. Insufficient power or space does not complete a partial batch.\n\nConnect to an xuxu Brewing Barrel with the Transfer Line in either order. Existing empty bottles automatically fill available barrel slots; full destinations retain stock in the printer. The barrel's linked print button uses this printer and its battery at the same batch cost. A connection alone does not continuously print new bottles.

Insert a charged battery and select a print button. Level 1 prints 6L Small Bottles for 20kJ each. None of these bottles accepts a filter. Water-level artwork updates with water amount.

Put this mod's or native seeds in input and a charged battery in the power slot. Each night seeds are processed top to bottom, then left to right. Each own seed produces one fruit; each native seed produces two matching crops; output uses row-order free space.

Each machine handles up to 2 seeds per night by default. Basic, intermediate, and advanced brewing certificates raise this to 5, 7, and 18 respectively; only the highest tier applies. A productive night costs 12kJ per machine, not per fruit. Multiple machines settle independently.

Native Coffee Beans also count as seeds. Bloomberry produces native Wine Berries; Hydroreed produces two native filters. Outputs use fixed normal forms without hydroponic module bonuses or extra returned seeds. The nightly quota counts seeds consumed. Both native products must fit; insufficient space or power retains the seed. Both grids are 12×12 and permit rearranging accepted items. Hover the instruction note on the far right to read it.
